docRepo.head: 3e06bdc
docRepo.note: Not written to by this lane except this checkpoint set; pre-existing staged/unstaged state in this worktree belongs to other in-flight sessions and was not touched.

workRepo.registeredIn: _catalog/seat_register.json seats[govtech].repos[plan-review] (no branch pinned by design; this seat ships per-PR feature branches)
workRepo.note: The worktree's prior checked-out branch (govtech/g-113-seam-vocabulary) was already merged into origin/main (confirmed: git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/govtech/g-113-seam-vocabulary origin/main -> MERGED) and origin/main had moved one commit further (G-114, #13) by the time this lane started. New branch cut from the current tip, not the stale checked-out one.

missionPremise: Mission _inbox/2026-09-02_g115_tenant_and_icc_wiring_mission.md, items 1 and 4 of the Bastrop PermitFlow island-cut WDLL (approved 2026-09-02). Item 1: register a real bastrop_tx persona and prove cross-tenant engagement reads are refused, the same live-violation standard G-106 used for Smart Files. Item 4: wire IBC2018P6's code lookup to the real, already-ingested substrate content instead of its frozen-empty static manifest, while leaving IPMC2018P2 (confirmed no real content) alone.
completionPredicate: A stranger can (a) create an engagement as bastrop_tx/staff and see orgId=bastrop_tx on the row, (b) attempt to read that engagement as template-city/staff and get refused, and the reverse, both proven against the live deployed service, not just a unit test; (c) request a real, live-ingested IBC section number and get a resolved citation sourced from the substrate atom, not a typed absence; (d) request a genuinely non-existent or non-entitled section and still get a typed, correctly-classified absence; (e) confirm IPMC2018P2's existing honest-empty behaviour is unchanged.
scopeBasis: Bounded to items 1 and 4 only, per the mission's own scope boundary: items 2/3/5/6 depend on this landing first or are the operator's own action. smartcity-os is never touched (absolute no-touch, unrelated to this repo anyway). G-52 is not started (different, still-blocked row). The absence taxonomy's spelling/shape (G-113) is read but not altered.

investigationFindings.item1ExistingGap: Read store.mjs and server.mjs's whole engMatch block (GET/POST /api/plan-review/engagements/:id and every nested route -- matrix, briefing, letter, map-feature, documents, sheets, dataroom-atoms, override, share, edition). getEngagement/listEngagements/findEngagementByFolder take NO org filter at all; every nested route hangs off one unscoped fetch. GET /api/plan-review/reviewer/engagements (listEngagements) has no persona concept whatsoever and is left alone deliberately -- it is the Empressa-internal cross-tenant reviewer queue by original design (icc-demo/reviewer), not a defect this mission's check names.
investigationFindings.item1IdentityMechanism: web/app.js's api() helper has ALWAYS sent the caller's persona as an `x-persona: <orgId>/<userId>` header on every request (read for smartFilesScopeRefusal in web/api/backend.js), but backend.js's proxy handler never forwarded that header to the actual plan-review Cloud Run backend -- it was read and then dropped. This is the actual mechanism used: no new header scheme, no query-param convention invented; the existing header is now forwarded, and server.mjs reads it.
investigationFindings.item1PriorArt: G-106 (smart-files read-path scope, closed 2026-09-02) and its own smartFilesScopeRefusal function are the direct model: a pure function returning null (allow) or {status, body} (refuse), keyed on an asserted-but-unverified persona string -- 'a narrowing, not a closure', explicitly not an auth system. engagementCrossTenantRefusal (actors.mjs) mirrors that shape and that same caveat.
investigationFindings.item4LiveContentConfirmed: Live get_atom against did:hauska:code-section:icc-model-code/2018-international-building-code-6th-printing/1001-1 (section 1001.1), with the plan-review-platform-key secret (already wired as HAUSKA_MCP_PLATFORM_KEY for G-112), returns a real, section-shaped atom. list_jurisdictions shows jurisdictionTenant icc-model-code, atomCount 4966. Anonymous get_atom on the same DID returns 'not readable under the caller's accessPolicy' -- confirms the key is required, matches the mission's 'codex-tier key' framing (the enforcement is per-atom accessPolicy, not a tool-tier gate -- get_atom itself is described as public Layer 1 in tools/list; the ICC atom's own accessPolicy is what requires a key).
investigationFindings.item4DidMapping: Dot-to-dash section-number mapping confirmed against the live call: 1001.1 -> DID suffix 1001-1. A well-formed but non-existent DID (9999-1) returns a clean 200 {"data":{"atom":null},...,"meta":{"note":"No atom found..."}}, not an error -- a positive determination, distinct from a fetch failure.
investigationFindings.item4IpmcConfirmedEmpty: hauska-mcp-server's own plan_review_get_code tool (tools/list) describes itself: 'Codex (plan review): GET a code-library citation. IPMC is a typed absence.' Independently, get_atom probes against plausible IPMC section DIDs found nothing, and search_atoms/query_jurisdiction expose no per-edition breakdown that would show otherwise. Two independent signals agree: IPMC2018P2 gets no live path in this change.
investigationFindings.incidentalDefectFound: get_atom's real response nests section fields one level deeper than the existing route's payload extraction (`atom?.data || atom?.atom || atom`) reaches: the real shape is {"data":{"atom":{"title":...}}}, not {"data":{"title":...}}. Confirmed against BOTH a real IBC atom and the already-shipped Bastrop UDC 14-02-003 atom, keyed. This means the CURRENTLY DEPLOYED production route (pre-this-change) has been silently serving source-unavailable for every resolved section, including the Bastrop UDC ones shipped under G-108 -- confirmed directly against the live deployed revision (plan-review-ozx33wafia-ue.a.run.app) before writing any fix: BASTROP-UDC/14-02-003 returned {"absence":{"status":"source-unavailable"...}} in production. This is a necessary fix for item 4's own check to be satisfiable (the new IBC live path shares the same extraction code) and is folded into this change rather than filed as a separate card, since it blocks the exact feature being built and is a one-line extraction-order correction, not a restructuring.
investigationFindings.substrateInconsistencyNoted_notFixed: list_jurisdictions reports icc-model-code and bastrop_tx as accessPolicy 'public-free' at the jurisdiction-rollup level, but per-atom get_atom enforcement refuses BOTH anonymously (confirmed on a real Bastrop UDC atom, not just ICC). Two independently derived signals disagree (jurisdiction rollup vs per-atom enforcement). Not this repo's defect to fix (hauska-mcp-server is substrate-seat owned); named here as an incidental finding, not corrected.

designDecisionsAndRejectedAlternatives.why: Matches the existing convention already in this file's own CODE_BOOKS['BASTROP-UDC'] (editionId bastrop_tx-bdc-2026-adopted, publisher bastrop_tx) rather than inventing a new slug, per the mission's own instruction to check for precedent first.

designDecisionsAndRejectedAlternatives.decision: Identity via the existing x-persona header (forwarded through backend.js), not a new query-param scheme.
designDecisionsAndRejectedAlternatives.rejected: Threading orgId/userId as new query params on every engagement GET call site in web/app.js.
designDecisionsAndRejectedAlternatives.why: The header already flows end-to-end from every api() call once a persona is set locally; the only broken link was the BFF silently dropping it. Reusing it is a 2-line fix in one file plus a header read in server.mjs, versus retrofitting ~10 call sites in app.js with no way to browser-test the result in this environment. Matches 'reuse existing data and component mapping' from the mission's standing constraints.

designDecisionsAndRejectedAlternatives.decision: The refusal fires only when a persona is asserted; an unscoped (no-persona) read passes through unchanged.
designDecisionsAndRejectedAlternatives.why: Operator ruling explicitly scoped this pilot to the existing named-persona access model, not a new auth build. The internal reviewer/QA path (icc-demo/reviewer seeing across tenants) is existing, deliberate product behaviour, not this mission's defect. Closing that would be a distinct, larger change.

designDecisionsAndRejectedAlternatives.decision: No fabricated IBC Pass/Fail row added to matrixFromChain.
designDecisionsAndRejectedAlternatives.rejected: Interpreting the check's 'live matrix run ... returns a genuine Pass/Fail' as requiring a new adjudicated IBC row in the 4-row compliance matrix.
designDecisionsAndRejectedAlternatives.why: No real adjudicable dimension exists for IBC content in this engagement model today (the only submitted numeric dimension, proposedSetbackFrontFt, is Bastrop-UDC-specific). Inventing one would fabricate a comparison with nothing behind it. The mission's own body text is unambiguous about what to build (a live query path in code-lookup.mjs feeding the existing /api/plan-review/code route, exactly the shape the UDC path already has) and is treated as authoritative over one ambiguous phrase in the check bullet; the check is satisfied via that route's resolved-vs-typed-absence discriminator instead, and this is stated explicitly rather than silently reinterpreted.

Two independent live signals (the substrate's own tool description, and failed get_atom probes) confirm no real content exists. Wiring a live path with nothing behind it would add complexity for a book with nothing to serve.

adversarialPreBuildCheck.q1_couldTheCrossTenantCheckBeVacuouslySa: Only if the refusal function refused everything (including same-org reads) or refused nothing. Both are named test cases before any implementation is trusted (mirrors backend.test.mjs's own 'the gate is not vacuous in either direction' pattern for G-106).
adversarialPreBuildCheck.q2_couldTheLiveIbcPathBeVacuouslySatisfi: Only if every section resolved (no real absence ever reachable) or none did (the live path never actually fires). Both directions are named as required tests before trusting the implementation, plus a third failure mode specific to this design: an R-prefixed/non-numeric input must NOT spend a live call at all (pure no-I/O contract preserved for shapes that were never going to be real IBC content).
adversarialPreBuildCheck.q3_whatWouldMakeMeWrongAboutTheExtractio: If mcpCall()'s textPayload() already unwrapped one level before returning (making atom.data the section object directly). Read textPayload() in full: it only JSON.parses the raw text block once, no further unwrapping -- rejected. Confirmed instead by direct evidence: curling the real MCP server for both a real IBC atom and the already-shipped Bastrop UDC atom and observing the actual nested shape, then curling the LIVE DEPLOYED production route (before writing any fix) and observing it return source-unavailable for a section its own manifest claims is ingested -- two independent confirmations, not one inference.
adversarialPreBuildCheck.q4_whatBypassesTheRefusal: A caller that never sends x-persona (unchanged pass-through, by design, not a bypass of what this closes). A future direct-to-Cloud-Run caller with a valid PLAN_REVIEW_SERVICE_TOKEN but no x-persona header still reads unscoped -- this is the 'narrowing not closure' the docstring states explicitly, matching G-106's own stated posture.

constraintsToHonor: Live Bastrop (smartcity-os) stays untouched -- not read, not written; this mission is a separate repo entirely.
Additive only: CODE_BOOKS, AVAILABLE_EDITIONS, buildCitation()/renderCitationText(), the absence taxonomy's kinds and spelling all stay exactly as-is in shape.
No new auth system for item 1.
PoC license constraint: no verbatim ICC body text ever surfaced; the existing quotable-gate on `analysis` (false for ICC books) is left exactly as it is.
